#6425 downloads the four `ocean_large_eddy_simulation_DynamicSmagorinsky_*` regression files from a branch on a contributor's fork. That branch can be deleted or force-pushed at any time, and CI would load whatever it then contains.

The same files are now in `glwagner/OceananigansArtifacts.jl` (merged in glwagner/OceananigansArtifacts.jl#11). This PR points `dynamic_smagorinsky_path` at that repository, pinned to the merge commit `1f2eedd`, so the reference data can no longer change underneath the tests.

The files at the pinned URL are byte-identical to the ones on the fork branch, so `regression_truth_data_v4` keeps its name and cached copies on CI remain valid.

body:
When a time window spans more time indices than a partly in-memory `FieldTimeSeries` holds, `update_field_time_series!` throws an
`ArgumentError` that gives the times and the indices but not the series. A model with several series (forcing, restoring, radiation) on 32
ranks prints 32 interleaved copies of it, and finding which series failed took a separate investigation. The message now starts with
`summary(fts)`:

```
ArgumentError: 2×2×2×5 FieldTimeSeries{InMemory} located at (Center, Center, Center) of c at …/c.jld2: times 0.5 to 2.5 span time
indices 1 to 4, more than the 2 held in memory; increase `time_indices_in_memory`.
```

Changes:

- The window error is prefixed with `summary(fts)`.

The split-explicit free surface asks every series for the whole barotropic substep window. When a time node falls inside the window, the
window spans three indices, so a backend of two fails at the first such node. The OMIP run that hit this had a chlorophyll series of
two in memory, and it died at model day 45.5, when the mid-February SeaWiFS node fell inside the substep window. NumericalEarth's
dataset-backed series default to three indices since v0.9.4.

body:
The zero-argument `versioninfo_with_gpu()` branches on `isdefined(Main, :CUDA)`. On Julia ≥ 1.12, inference folds this check and records an
edge on the `Main.CUDA` binding, so `using CUDA` in `Main` invalidates `initialize_nc_file` / `initialize_zarr_store!` and every caller above
them (`initialize!` of the writers, `write_output!`, `time_step!(::Simulation)`, `run!`). Precompiled workloads that include these methods
are recompiled at load time. Reported by @daverumph, who measured 229 s of recompilation per launch.

Changes:

- `versioninfo_with_gpu()` is removed. The NetCDF and Zarr writers call `versioninfo_with_gpu(child_architecture(architecture(model)))`, and
  one generic method `versioninfo_with_gpu(arch) = ""` covers every architecture without a specific method, so `Distributed`, Metal, AMD,
  oneAPI and Reactant models keep writing output. `Distributed` CUDA models report the CUDA device as before.
- The CUDA method drops an unused `s = sprint(versioninfo)` and the `InteractiveUtils` import it needed.

Changed output: in a session that loads CUDA, a CPU model writes `"This file was generated using "` in the `Julia` attribute, where it wrote
the CUDA device name. `versioninfo_with_gpu(CPU())` returns `""` where it returned `"No GPU device"`. Files written by CPU-only sessions and
by CUDA models are unchanged.

title: Take the GPU in output metadata from the model's architecture

body:
`Checkpointer` writes to `joinpath(dir, prefix * "_iteration$(iteration).jld2")`, but `pickup` globs `prefix * "_iteration*.jld2"` inside
`dir`. When `prefix` carries a directory, for example `prefix = joinpath(output_directory, "run_checkpoint")`, writing works because
`joinpath(".", "/absolute/path")` drops the `"."`. The glob pattern then starts with `/`, though, and pickup throws
`Glob pattern cannot be empty or start with a / character`, and only at the first restart.

Changes:

- The constructor splits `joinpath(dir, prefix)` into `dir` and `prefix`, so a directory given in `prefix` moves into `dir`.
  Checkpoints land at the same paths as before, so files written before the change are picked up after it. A prefix without a directory
  gives the same `dir` and `prefix` as before.
- `mkpath` also creates a directory given in `prefix`.
- New test: checkpoint with a directory in `prefix`, then pick up from it. On main it fails with the `Glob` error above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Find checkpoints written with a directory in the Checkpointer prefix

body:
On a grid with a single vertical level the vertical halo is one cell. Building a `PartialCellBottom` (or `PartialCellVerticalBoundaries`) grid there throws a `BoundsError` if any column is fully immersed:

- a land column (bottom at the top) has `⌊s⌋ = Nz + 1`, so the bottom face reciprocal is computed at face `Nz + 2`;
- a column fully covered by the top boundary has `⌊s⌋ = 0`, so `Δrᶜᶜᶠ` at face 0 reads the cell spacing at `k = -1`.

Both indices lie outside a one-cell halo. That reciprocal is only read at the partial cell, which a fully immersed column doesn't have, so this PR clamps the face index to `1:Nz+1`. Columns that aren't fully immersed are unaffected.

The new test `test_single_level_partial_cells` (in `test/unit/immersed_boundary_grid.jl`) builds both cases on a one-level grid. With bounds checking on, it fails on `main` and passes with this change.

This came up in #6450, whose new test hit the bug.

title: Fix out-of-bounds partial-cell spacings in fully immersed columns on single-level grids

Reactant v0.2.309 fails to compile the Enzyme gradient through the checkpointed `@trace` loop in `test/reactant/tripolar.jl` (`operand #0 does not dominate this use`). This has turned the Reactant jobs red on `main` and on every PR since Nov 23. This caps Reactant at 0.2.308 in the test environment only, so users of the extension can still take newer versions.

Upstream: EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl#3842. Lift the cap once that is fixed.
